instructions: Finely chop the onion and slice the garlic. Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.

Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and add 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, beat the eggs in a bowl with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Grate the pecorino. That should be about 1/2 cup.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour in half the eggs. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, pulling the set edges toward the center and tilting the pan so the raw egg runs underneath, until the bottom is golden and the top is nearly set.
Slide the frittata onto a plate. Turn the pan upside down over the plate, flip them together, and cook the other side for 1 minute. Transfer it to a cutting board.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same skillet and make a second frittata the same way with the rest of the eggs.
Cut each frittata in half, then slice into strips about 1 inch wide.
Tear 1/4 cup of mint leaves. Stir the strips and the mint into the tomatoes over medium heat. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes, until the sauce clings to the eggs.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve in shallow bowls with the pecorino on top.
method_notes: Pasta Grammar's Uova in Trippa alla Romana is the lead (no ratings on the page, so this is a fallback): a plain onion and tomato sauce, a thin frittata cut into strips, then mint and cheese. Another page (Food Republic/Getrecipecart) uses garlic, a 28 oz can of tomatoes and 8 eggs for 4 people, which this follows for the amounts. Cheese varies by cook; this uses pecorino as the dish description says. The sources use 4 thin frittatas; this makes 2 thicker ones to fit the time. Chili flakes left out to keep the base mild.
